current_bottleneck: Global temperature proves the model is under-dispersed in aggregate, but scalar widening is not a solution. Temperature 1.10 and 1.15 improve horizon coverage and bad-window rate but reduce the broad-frame score to 4/11 by damaging tail-shape/time-series, cointegration or pathwise subtests, level KS, median bias, and conditionality. Regime layer2 remains 0/8. The missing component is conditional allocation/location, not global noise.
last_result_summary: 597a evaluated 510a final on the 441-window broad frame at sample_temperature 1.10 and 1.15. Temp 1.10 scored 4/11: coverage90 improved to 73.4%, bad-window rate to 18.6%, pathwise max-jump KS to 0.321, but cointegration worst-cell fell to 0.239, level KS to 2/25, and time_series still failed. Temp 1.15 scored 4/11: coverage90 improved to 75.0%, bad-window rate to 18.4%, persistent undercoverage to 13.8%, pathwise max-jump KS to 0.258, but tail-scale cells collapsed to 15/25 and pathwise realism failed. Both keep regime layer2 at 0/8 and worsen conditionality/worst-cell MAE.
next_step_recommendation: Close global temperature as a learned-model solution. Do not add another source-noise knob: 448a-450a already capped conditional scale heads, and 597a caps scalar temperature. The next principled step is a paradigm decision: either accept a risk-policy overlay for stress use, or move beyond IV-only state by training the same unified factor generator with genuinely informative joint factors so the model can learn where future level mass belongs.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a and 596a both score 5/11, but 510a is the better risk profile because 596a narrows coverage and worsens distributional fidelity. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product.
